questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD proficiency in namespace scoping, ConfigMap/Secret wiring, InitContainer usage, persistent logging, DLQ handling, and monitoring hooks.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped ConfigMaps and Secrets
- InitContainer to install curl
- Deployment with a worker loop
- PVC-backed logs and DLQ
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- HorizontalPodAutoscaler by CPU

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: traffic-gen
  namespace: example-ns
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: traffic-gen
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: traffic-gen
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-curl
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl && mkdir -p /logs/dlq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: curlimages/curl:8.1.2
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: traffic-config
        - secretRef:
            name: traffic-secret
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: traffic-logs-pvc
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to patch multi-resource manifests and reason about rolling updates and resourcing in real deployments.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers for bootstrapping binaries
- PVC data paths and volume mounts
- Probes for correctness
- HorizontalPodAutoscaler and resource requests/limits

- ConfigMap-triggered restarts via annotations

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: stream-processor
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/configqueue: queue-version-hash
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-binary
          image: alpine
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - wget -O /usr/local/bin/processor http://assets.local/processor.bin && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/processor
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data-input
              mountPath: /data/input
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: myregistry/stream-processor:latest
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
      volumes:
        - name: data-input
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: stream-processor-input
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD mastery of multi-resource coordination, init containers, volumes, secrets, and network policies. It also validates per-namespace config management and safe log persistence.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob and Job orchestration across a namespace
- InitContainer to install client tooling and share /tools
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for migrations and DB credentials
- PVC-backed /logs for auditability
- NetworkPolicy restricting egress to Postgres
- Status tracking in a namespace ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
spec:
  schedule: "*/12 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          - name: migrations
            configMap:
              name: migrations-config
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client && mkdir -p /tools && cp /usr/bin/psql /tools/psql"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
          containers:
          - name: migrate
            image: migrate-base:latest
            command: ["/tools/psql","-h","$(DB_HOST)","-U","$(DB_USER)","-d","$(DB_NAME)","-f","/migrations/*.sql"]
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-credentials
            - configMapRef:
                name: db-config
            volumeMounts:
            - name: migrations
              mountPath: /migrations
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs
- InitContainer size vs main image size; tooling duplication
- Per-namespace migrations risk drift vs centralized control
- Secret rotation complexity; ensure timely updates
- Logging volume retention vs cost

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical CKAD skills including per-namespace configuration management, InitContainer usage, sidecar patterns, secure secret handling, and network policy implementation.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace deployments with shared persistent volumes
- InitContainer for runtime dependency installation
- Inotify-based file change detection and yamllint validation
- In-service reload capabilities (nginx -s reload)
- ConfigMap and Secret integration patterns
- TLS sidecar implementation for secure communications
- Namespace-level NetworkPolicy for egress restrictions

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton of the Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-watcher
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-watcher
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-watcher
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache inotify-tools yamllint']
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:alpine
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-pvc
          mountPath: /config/dynamic
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
      - name: config-watcher
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'while inotifywait -e modify /config/dynamic/*.yaml; do yamllint /config/dynamic/*.yaml && nginx -s reload; done']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-pvc
          mountPath: /config/dynamic
        env:
        - name: STATUS_URL
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: status-secret
              key: url
      - name: tls-sidecar
        image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
      volumes:
      - name: config-pvc
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: config-pvc
      - name: nginx-defaults
        configMap:
          name: nginx-defaults
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: config-pvc
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-defaults
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    # Default Nginx configuration
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: status-secret
  namespace: target-namespace
type: Opaque
data:
  url: aHR0cDovL3N0YXR1cy5sb2NhbC9hcGkvdjEvcmVsb2Fk
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: config-watcher-netpol
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-watcher
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: internal-services
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
```

## Trade-offs
- **Inotify vs polling**: Inotify is more efficient but requires file system support
- **Sidecar overhead**: TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource usage
- **Single namespace scope**: Limited to namespace-level isolation vs cluster-wide
- **PVC dependency**: Requires storage management and backup strategies
- **Container sharing**: Process communication within pod vs separate services

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: PVC handling, InitContainers, ConfigMaps/Secrets, simple templating, manifest validation, and network policies. It avoids previous questions by focusing on label injection and re-validation flow.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer tool installation (kubeval, yamllint)
- ConfigMap/Secret usage for config and credentials
- PVC-mounted manifest discovery and simple file loop
- Lightweight templating to inject labels
- Validation with kubeval/yamllint and conditional POST
- TLS sidecar and readiness/liveness probes
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy restricting egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: manifest-tagger
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: manifest-tagger
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache kubeval yamllint curl jq && echo done"]
      containers:
      - name: tagger
        image: your-registry/manifest-tagger:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
        - name: tagged
          mountPath: /tagged
        - name: config
          mountPath: /config
        env:
        - name: TAG_KEY
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: tagger-config
              key: tag-key
        - name: API_BASE
          value: http://tagger-portal:8080/api/v1/summary
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      - name: tls-sidecar
        image: curlimages/curl:7.88.1
        # TLS rotation logic assumed
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: manifests-pvc
      - name: tagged
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: tagger-config
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the end-to-end flow locally? 
- How would you handle a manifest that fails validation after tagging? 
- How would you scale if the namespace has hundreds of manifests per minute?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates CKAD-ready knowledge of CronJob patterns, PVCs, Secrets, InitContainers, health checks, and NetworkPolicy in a realistic data-processing workflow.

## Key Concepts

- **CronJob and Job lifecycle**: Understanding scheduling, concurrency policies, and job history limits
- **PVC mounts**: Using persistent volumes for input, output, and log storage within a namespace
- **Secrets**: Securely storing and mounting authentication tokens
- **InitContainers**: Pre-installing required tooling (awk, coreutils) before the main container runs
- **Readiness and Liveness probes**: Ensuring the pod is ready to serve traffic and remains healthy
- **NetworkPolicy**: Enforcing namespace-level egress restrictions to a central endpoint
- **Idempotent processing**: Handling file transformations safely across runs
- **Log management**: Persisting logs to PVC for debugging and auditing

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-transform
  namespace: data-processing
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: debian:book-slim
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apt-get update && apt-get install -y awk coreutils && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
          containers:
          - name: transformer
            image: alpine:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
            args:
            - |-
              apk add --no-cache curl awk
              for f in /input/*; do
                [ -f "$f" ] || continue
                awk '{print $0}' "$f" > "/output/$(basename $f)"
              done
              curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $(cat /secrets/token)" -d "@/logs/summary.json" https://central-endpoint.example.com/api/summary
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /ready
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /health
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            volumeMounts:
            - name: input
              mountPath: /input
            - name: output
              mountPath: /output
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: token-secret
              mountPath: /secrets
              readOnly: true
          volumes:
          - name: input
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: input-pvc
          - name: output
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: output-pvc
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          - name: token-secret
            secret:
              secretName: api-token-secret
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress
  namespace: data-processing
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: central-endpoint
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

## Trade-offs

- **InitContainer vs. custom image**: Using an InitContainer adds startup overhead but keeps the main image lightweight. A custom image with pre-installed tools eliminates this but increases maintenance.
- **ConcurrencyPolicy**: Using `Forbid` prevents overlapping jobs, simplifying idempotency but may cause missed runs if a job takes too long.
- **PVC vs. emptyDir**: PVCs provide persistence and data sharing across job runs but require proper storage provisioning. emptyDir is simpler but ephemeral.
- **NetworkPolicy granularity**: Restricting egress to specific pods enhances security but requires careful label management and may break if endpoints change.
- **Probe implementation**: HTTP probes require an endpoint; exec probes are more flexible but add complexity.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose Kubernetes primitives for practical automation: CronJobs, Jobs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and PVCs, plus robust scheduling and rollback.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and jobTemplate usage
- ConfigMap and Secret as environment sources
- PVC mounting in Jobs for persistent backups
- Concurrency policy and job history controls
- Rollback and validation workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: db-backup
  namespace: dataops
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 7
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: postgres-backup
            image: postgres:15
            env:
            - name: BACKUP_DIR
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: BACKUP_DIR
            - name: DB_HOST
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: backup-config
                  key: DB_HOST
            - name: DB_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_USER
            - name: DB_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: db-credentials
                  key: DB_PASSWORD
            command:
            - /bin/bash
            - -c
            - |
              DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)
              BACKUP_FILE="/backups/${DB_NAME}-${DATE}.sql"
              pg_dump -h $DB_HOST -U $DB_USER -d $DB_NAME > $BACKUP_FILE
            volumeMounts:
            - name: backup-storage
              mountPath: /backups
          volumes:
          - name: backup-storage
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Validation Plan
1. Check CronJob creation: `kubectl get cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Verify schedule: `kubectl describe cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
3. Test manual job: `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/db-backup test-backup -n dataops`
4. Monitor job completion: `kubectl get jobs -n dataops -w`
5. Validate backup files: `kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n dataops -- ls -la /backups`

## Rollback Plan
1. Delete CronJob: `kubectl delete cronjob db-backup -n dataops`
2. Clean up test jobs: `kubectl delete jobs -l job-name=db-backup -n dataops`
3. Remove backup files if needed: Access PVC and delete specific backup files
4. Recreate with corrected manifest if issues persist

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and runtime verification in CKAD scope, including namespace policies, container security, probes, and network controls.

## Key Concepts
- PodSecurity via namespace labels
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities
- Probes: readiness and liveness
- PreStop lifecycle
- ConfigMap mounting and rolling restarts via checksum
- NetworkPolicy egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch sketch (Deployment + NetworkPolicy)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: logger
  namespace: logging
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: logger
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: logger
        image: registry.example/logger:1.0
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cfg
          mountPath: /etc/logger
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /livez
            port: 8080
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
      volumes:
      - name: cfg
        configMap:
          name: logger-config
```

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: logger-egress
  namespace: logging
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: logger
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9200
```

Why This Is Asked
- Tests practical CKAD skills: PVC-based file intake, in-cluster validation, batch processing, and external posting. Includes init tooling, secret handling, TLS rotation, and network policies.

Key Concepts
- PVC-based file discovery in a Deployment
- InitContainer for tooling installation
- kubectl dry-run validation and yamllint
- Batch processing controlled by a ConfigMap value
- Secrets for API credentials and TLS sidecar rotation
- NetworkPolicy scoping to internal endpoints
- Rollback and observability strategies

Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for the auditor Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: auditor
  namespace: audit
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: auditor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: auditor
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: audits
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: audits-pvc
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: audit-config
      initContainers:
        - name: prep-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache kubectl yamllint curl; sleep 0"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: audits
              mountPath: /audits
      containers:
        - name: auditor
          image: registry.example/auditor:latest
          volumeMounts:
            - name: audits
              mountPath: /audits
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/audit
          env:
            - name: AUDIT_ENDPOINT
              value: "http://audit-portal:8080/api/v1/audit"
          readinessProbe: {"tcpSocket": {"port": 8080}, "initialDelaySeconds": 15, "periodSeconds": 10}
          livenessProbe: {"tcpSocket": {"port": 8080}, "initialDelaySeconds": 30, "periodSeconds": 20}
      tolerations: []
```
